bead.title: Document the cross-backend scenario rule for new engine ports
bead.description:
PROBLEM
Nothing written down told the epic that shipped CommitTransitionPort (pqueue-2201fd37) that a new port needs a pqueue-conformance scenario, not a bespoke per-backend test file. The crate-level "no-stub" philosophy is documented (crates/pqueue-conformance/src/lib.rs module doc) but does not say this explicitly, so the same gap can recur for the next new port (e.g. a future DiscoveryPort-style addition).

PROPOSED FIX
Add a short, explicit rule to the pqueue-conformance module doc (crates/pqueue-conformance/src/lib.rs top comment, alongside the existing conformance matrix table): any new engine port intended for more than one backend MUST add a capability-gated scenario to pqueue-conformance (positive behavioral proof when advertised, explicit-decline + capability-flag-consistency proof when not) rather than a bespoke test file scoped to a single backend crate. Cite the CommitTransitionPort gap (this epic) as the concrete precedent for why the rule exists.

IN-SCOPE FILES
- crates/pqueue-conformance/src/lib.rs (module doc only)

OUT-OF-SCOPE
- Any code changes.
- Auditing other ports for the same gap (separate follow-up if wanted; the hot-projection substrate's `*_capabilities_are_explicit` convention is already a reasonable analog, not this bead's problem to re-litigate).
bead.acceptance:
1. `rg -n 'MUST add a.*scenario|conformance scenario' crates/pqueue-conformance/src/lib.rs` finds the new rule text.
2. `cargo fmt --check` passes (doc-comment-only change, but keep the gate for consistency).
